The increasing adoption of image-guided robot-assisted surgery (IGS) in retinal operations has created a demand for automated visual navigation systems. This study presents a novel method for automatically identifying and localizing anatomical landmarks within OCT angiography (OCTA) images. The approach utilizes a convolutional neural network (CNN) trained on a dataset of 1,000 manually annotated images to detect key points. To enhance the model's performance, a specialized loss function was developed, and the architecture was optimized through a multi-step process involving ablation studies and hyperparameter tuning. The results demonstrate that this method surpasses existing techniques, achieving a mean localization error of 0.19 mm, with a 95% confidence interval of 0.13–0.24 mm.

We derive the $F$-polynomials associated with cluster algebras linked to surfaces by utilizing combinatorial models involving triangulated surfaces decorated with marked points. This approach extends a finding originally made by Lee.

The rise of the web has introduced a widespread yet problematic authentication system that relies on passwords. This paper explores the concept of a passwordless web, specifically focusing on the challenges and opportunities involved in eliminating passwords entirely. We argue that while removing passwords completely is unfeasible in the immediate future, significant progress can be achieved by offering robust passwordless alternatives.

Discrete lattice models are frequently approximated using a compact continuous momentum space, a method that, despite its utility, is known to yield inaccurate results. This study introduces a novel continuous momentum space that is noncompact yet possesses a discrete spectrum, which can serve as a precise framework for describing discrete lattices. The proposed approach is demonstrated through the analysis of the one-dimensional tight-binding model, as well as the two-dimensional square and honeycomb models. Furthermore, it is established that this momentum space can be explicitly realized by a discrete phase space, linking it to the Weyl quantization formalism.

The design of autoplay within video applications can inadvertently undermine user agency, frequently leading to adverse outcomes. This report examines the ethical complexities surrounding this feature, specifically addressing its impact on user control and well-being. We begin by reviewing the current landscape of video apps, detailing how autoplay is implemented and its resulting effects on user autonomy. Subsequently, we propose design principles aimed at restoring user agency, offering concrete examples that prioritize ethical considerations. Finally, we conclude by highlighting unresolved issues and proposing future research directions.

This work examines the operational semantics of a specific subset of reactive Turing machines, a framework encompassing a broad spectrum of practical reactive systems. We define behaviours for such machines as infinite sequences of state-action pairs and introduce the concepts of executability and finite executability to these behaviours. Specifically, a behaviour is finitely executable if each action within it corresponds to a reachable state in a finite execution sequence. We demonstrate that every finitely executable behaviour is executable and further prove that a reactive Turing machine admits only finitely many finitely executable behaviours. Additionally, we show that a behaviour is executable if and only if it is finitely executable whenever all transitions in the machine are deterministic.

A combinatorial Gray code represents a sequential arrangement of combinatorial objects where successive items differ by minimal alteration. While numerous such sequences exist for various structures like partitions, set partitions, and spanning trees, this paper introduces a novel methodology for constructing them. The core of our approach relies on a specific transformation connecting partitions to spanning trees, enabling a sequence of partitions to be derived from a sequence of spanning trees. We further provide an algorithm that generates all partitions of a given integer $n$ within $O(1)$ time per element (amortized), matching the efficiency of standard spanning tree Gray codes.

Its primary objectives include measuring the energy loss of high-transverse-momentum particles traversing dense media, analyzing jet quenching, and determining the partonic composition of nuclear matter. This study introduces a space-time finite element framework designed for the incompressible Navier-Stokes equations within moving domains. The proposed method ensures conforming discretization of space-time elements by maintaining alignment between the domain boundaries and mesh interfaces, thereby eliminating spurious numerical boundary fluxes. The approach partitions the space-time continuum into multiple slabs, solving the Navier-Stokes system independently within each. To address the temporal evolution, a staggered time discretization is employed, where velocity and pressure are approximated at distinct time instances. The resulting discrete scheme is rigorously proven to be well-posed, and a corresponding algorithm is developed. Numerical experiments validate the theoretical findings and demonstrate the efficacy of the method in handling time-dependent simulations involving the space-time Navier-Stokes equations.

A circular flow index in a signed graph is defined as the maximum absolute value of the sum of vertices' labels, where each label is either 1 or -1, under the constraint that the product of labels for every triangle equals one. We demonstrate that for any signed graph lacking both balanced and signed-triangle-free properties, the circular flow index is at least two-thirds of the graph's vertex count. Furthermore, we prove that only specific exceptional signed graphs achieve this minimum value.

We introduce a Monte-Carlo randomized algorithm that solves the Modular Subset Sum problem in an expected $O(n \log^2 C)$ time complexity with a success probability of at least $1 - O(n^{-1})$. This approach improves upon the best-known deterministic algorithm, which requires $O(n \log^3 C)$ time.

Drosophila melanogaster serves as a premier model for investigating the development of the immune system, a system that is fully functional at birth. During embryogenesis, hemocytes are generated in the pericardial cavity and subsequently migrate to the ventral vessel to initiate the formation of a blood vessel. This paper introduces a novel approach for automatically segmenting hemocytes and their nuclei within live Drosophila embryos, utilizing a U-Net architecture. The system was trained on a dataset of 1,000 images, which were generated by applying data augmentation techniques to an original set of 100 images. The results demonstrate that the trained model achieves high accuracy in segmenting both hemocytes and their nuclei.

This paper introduces a contrastive Siamese network designed to extract robust speech features for end-to-end automatic speech recognition (ASR). The model employs a Siamese architecture paired with contrastive loss to force the embedding of acoustically similar frames closer in the latent space. Additionally, we integrate a novel self-attention mechanism that captures long-range temporal dependencies, and we utilize the contrastive loss to enhance the generalization capabilities of the embeddings. Evaluated on the LibriSpeech test set, our approach achieves a 4.7% Word Error Rate (WER) on the development subset and 4.8% on the evaluation subset.

This study introduces a novel scaling variable, $\xi_w$, designed to analyze the neutrino-nucleon scattering cross section. The theoretical framework for $\xi_w$ is derived from a combination of the parton distribution function (PDF) and the hard-scattering cross section. By integrating the PDFs with the factorization scale $Q^2$ and the cross-section calculation, we establish a new scaling variable that enables the cross section to be expressed as a function of $\xi_w$ alone. This approach allows for the investigation of how the cross section varies with $\xi_w$ while maintaining independence from $Q^2$. Furthermore, we examine the dependence of the cross section on $Q^2$ within the $\xi_w$ framework, utilizing the latest global PDF sets and employing the leading-order (LO) and next-to-leading-order (NLO) perturbative QCD (pQCD) methods.

This study examines the regularity of a stochastic system characterized by linear dynamics, unknown coefficients, and additive colored noise. The objective is to establish a set of feedback controls that ensures the time-average of the $p$-th power of the state variable remains finite in expectation. It is demonstrated that specific regularity conditions are met when employing a particular type of feedback control designed through a modified version of the Kalman filter, which also incorporates suitable gain adjustments.

Active inference has emerged as a leading framework for modeling the brain, yet it is typically formulated for Markov decision processes (MDPs), which are restricted to planning single-armed sequences. This study introduces a variant, called branching time active inference (BTAI), designed to handle branching scenarios. We demonstrate that the BTAI framework can be implemented using standard active inference algorithms. Furthermore, we apply this approach to a generative model of branching time language, showcasing its potential for modeling language through a new lens.

We investigate the movement of a localized baryon number density pulse through quark gluon plasma, assuming the system remains in local thermal equilibrium. The study utilizes the hydrodynamic framework to model the plasma's response, with the baryon pulse represented as a Gaussian distribution. We analyze the pulse's evolution across varying times and spacetime locations, demonstrating that its shape remains Gaussian throughout the process. The findings indicate that baryon number is convected by the plasma flow while diffusing over time; however, we observe that these effects are minor, suggesting that a dense initial baryon distribution can traverse the quark gluon plasma with limited deformation.

This paper investigates a specific Hamiltonian system with one degree of freedom, defined by $H = \frac{1}{2}(p^2 + q^2) + \frac{1}{6}q^4 + \frac{1}{2}\mu q^2$, where $\mu$ is a real parameter. We demonstrate that for $\mu < -1$, the system possesses an isochronous center, and conversely, $\mu > -1$, it does not.

This study examines the Lorenz system's dynamics by analyzing the similarity signature curve, which tracks how trajectories evolve across different regions of the phase space. We establish that this curve is both non-empty and compact, and we derive specific conditions regarding it. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the curve is not merely a single point, and we provide an analytical formula for it. These findings offer novel insights into Lorenz system dynamics and may serve as a foundation for investigating other dynamical systems.

This paper proves that the LAN (Local Asymptotic Normality) property holds for a specific class of models involving the continuous observation of a stochastic differential equation driven by a stable L\'evien process, within a regime where the noise intensity shrinks toward zero.

This study establishes Weyl's asymptotic law for spectra associated with non-self-adjoint Weyl Laplacians acting on flat vector bundles defined over compact hyperbolic surfaces. The associated boundary conditions are characterized by a periodic system of linear equations. Additionally, we demonstrate that Weyl's law remains valid in cases involving singular boundary conditions.

This study introduces FNetAR, a new causal language modeling algorithm that eliminates the self-attention mechanism in favor of a standard multi-layer recurrent architecture. FNetAR retains the self-attention capabilities of the Transformer but implements a simplified version that processes only the most recent $k$ tokens, thereby ensuring a constant computational complexity of $O(k)$ per time step. This approach enables the model to maintain a theoretical maximum sequence length of infinity. We further develop a novel training strategy that leverages the inherent recurrence of FNetAR to train sequences significantly longer than standard autoregressive models. Our experiments on the WikiText-103 and Wikipedia-300M datasets demonstrate that FNetAR outperforms the Transformer-XL baseline by 1.5% and 2.1%, respectively, while matching the performance of the GPT-2 124M model on WikiText-103.

This study examines the transition from the universe's deceleration phase to its acceleration phase, utilizing a generalized dark energy model within a flat FLRW framework. By employing a quintessence scalar field, the analysis derives the corresponding time-dependent solutions for the Hubble parameter, energy density, and equation of state. These results are subsequently compared with observational data from Type Ia supernovae, the Hubble diagram, and the Hubble constant.

This study introduces a game-theoretic framework for resource allocation within edge computing networks, specifically targeting Service Function Chain (SFC) requests. The proposed approach aims to minimize the total latency of SFC services by strategically distributing network resources. To achieve this, a multi-stage game is developed where the first stage involves a centralized allocation of virtual network functions (VNFs) across the network, while the second stage addresses the distribution of traffic flows. Within the first stage, a mechanism is designed to distribute VNFs among available network nodes, while the second stage utilizes a specific game-theoretic algorithm to determine optimal routing. The analysis demonstrates that the game possesses a pure-strategy Nash equilibrium, which can be reached efficiently via a best-response dynamic. Additionally, the study presents a method for configuring VNFs across nodes to ensure the system converges to a Nash equilibrium, thereby guaranteeing stable resource allocation.

We examine the quantum phase diagram of two-dimensional disordered superconductors under varying magnetic flux. Our analysis reveals a quantum phase transition among three distinct states: a topological superconductor, a diffusive thermal metal, and a localized normal metal. Furthermore, we establish that the thermal metal exhibits a robust quantum anomalous Hall effect. These results offer a pathway for investigating non-equilibrium topological phases within superconducting systems.

This study examines the relationship between happiness and the pursuit of happiness within depression research by analyzing Twitter data. We developed a method to identify tweets containing the "happiness goal" using a set of keywords, and subsequently employed a Naive Bayes classifier to detect depression-related goal pursuit. Our findings indicate a strong link between happiness and the pursuit thereof among users experiencing depression, suggesting that individuals on social media actively seek happiness even when clinically diagnosed with depression.

Dark matter remains a significant mystery in astrophysics, with numerous theoretical proposals, including axions, WIMPs, and sterile neutrinos, seeking to explain its nature. This study examines the potential of a novel 3+1 model for sterile neutrinos, which accounts for both the small mass of active neutrinos and the anomalous electron g-factor. We demonstrate that this framework can account for the electron's mass, the measured g-factor, and the recently reported 51 keV gamma-ray line from the Galactic Center, all while adhering to current experimental limits on sterile neutrino mixing.

This study details the magnetic structure of Na$_{4-\delta}$NiTeO$_{6}$, a material where Ni$^{2+}$ ions form a distorted rock-salt lattice. Neutron powder diffraction reveals that below the Néel temperature of 23.5 K, the Ni$^{2+}$ magnetic moments arrange into a commensurate, antiferromagnetic, c-axis modulated structure. The magnetic propagation vector is identified as (0, 0.5, 0.5), and the magnetic Bragg peaks are successfully indexed using a magnetic unit cell of 2 $\times$ 2 $\times$ 4.

This study introduces a framework for quantifying trust within IoT networks, specifically designed to evaluate the reliability of data originating from diverse sources. It begins by examining the inherent uncertainty arising from varying data origins, such as differing levels of trust and the presence of missing values. Building on this, the paper develops a method to assess uncertainty and determine the optimal level of data reduction required to minimize it. Furthermore, it explores the impact of data normalization on uncertainty and the mechanisms for enhancing overall network trust through normalization techniques. The proposed approach is validated using a case study involving a smart home environment.

This study addresses the challenge of interpolating a continuous function from data points that are distributed irregularly along a line, with a specific focus on the "Gibbs phenomenon," which manifests as oscillations near discontinuities. While spline methods are traditionally employed to mitigate these oscillations, their standard application in this irregular context often results in a lack of theoretical understanding regarding the optimal degree of the splines required. This paper introduces a rigorous theoretical framework for line interpolation using irregularly spaced splines, offering a method to determine the optimal degree. This theory is validated through numerical experiments, which also demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in resolving the Gibbs phenomenon.

This study examines four-dimensional Taub-NUT solutions within Einstein-$\varpi$ gravity, a framework extending Einstein-Maxwell theory by incorporating a U(1) vector field $\varpi$. We derive the corresponding solutions and analyze their properties, revealing that the black hole and cosmological sectors each admit both asymptotically flat and de Sitter geometries. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the Einstein-Maxwell system constitutes a specific subset of Einstein-$\varpi$ theory. In this limit, the black hole and cosmological sectors are restricted to asymptotically flat and de Sitter spacetimes, respectively.

In Information Retrieval (IR) contexts, accurately labeling multimedia content is crucial for training and assessing models. This paper introduces a comprehensive dataset of 1.2 million images, each annotated with a precise bounding box for every detected object. The dataset covers 1,700 object categories and is built upon a crowd-sourcing framework that leverages a specialized interface to gather high-quality annotations from contributors. We detail the data collection process, including the specific tools and evaluation metrics used to ensure annotation quality. Additionally, we demonstrate the dataset's utility by training a detection model and benchmarking it against existing publicly available resources.

The coexistence of numerous species within large ecosystems remains a fundamental biological mystery. While the classic theory of limiting similarity posits that niche overlap inhibits coexistence, recent findings suggest that spatial heterogeneity and niche construction can overcome this barrier. In this study, we introduce a novel framework for understanding species coexistence that integrates both spatial heterogeneity and active niche construction. Our approach models a large ecosystem as a network of interacting communities, where each community is further divided into subgroups representing distinct microhabitats. We demonstrate that this multi-layered structure creates a dynamic feedback loop: the spatial arrangement of communities influences how species evolve their strategies, while the resulting niche construction reshapes the community's spatial organization. We identify a critical threshold in the spatial complexity of the system; beyond this point, the model exhibits a sudden, non-linear transition from a homogeneous state to a highly diverse configuration. This mechanism provides a robust explanation for how extensive biodiversity can emerge and persist within large ecosystems.

Network attacks are prevalent in both natural and artificial systems, with a primary defense strategy being the removal of specific nodes. This process can trigger an "avalanche," where one initial failure cascades into subsequent failures, eventually compromising the entire network. This study examines the relationship between the effectiveness of an attack and the likelihood of initiating such an avalanche. We analyze the probability that a random attack initiates an avalanche exceeding a specific threshold size, denoted as $P(A > A_0)$. Our findings indicate that this probability is a convex function of the removed node's degree, $k$. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the tail of the avalanche size distribution follows a power law, with an exponent that varies based on the underlying distribution of node degrees.

This paper introduces a new task and dataset designed to probe text comprehension by analyzing the depth of understanding required to answer questions. We hypothesize that questions necessitating deeper insight will elicit more complex answers and stronger evidence of true comprehension. To address this, we developed a multi-stage task and the corresponding dataset. Our evaluation shows that models trained on our dataset achieve significant performance gains on standard comprehension benchmarks compared to baseline models. Additionally, we provide a detailed analysis of the dataset's characteristics.

In this work, we introduce a novel task and dataset aimed at probing text comprehension through the lens of answer depth regarding comprehension questions. We theorize that queries demanding deeper insight will require more complex responses and serve as stronger indicators of true understanding. To realize this, we devised a multi-stage task and generated the associated dataset. Our findings indicate that training models on our dataset yields substantially superior results on mainstream benchmarks relative to baseline models. Furthermore, we offer an extensive examination of the dataset's properties.

This study introduces a novel mixed finite element method for addressing time-harmonic elastic wave propagation in unbounded domains. To achieve this, we employ complex coordinate stretching within a Perfectly Matched Layer (PML) region to truncate the computational domain. The proposed framework utilizes a mixed formulation that integrates the primary stress tensor and displacement vector as fundamental variables. We further demonstrate the scheme's optimal convergence rates regarding the energy norm. Finally, numerical experiments are conducted to confirm the theoretical findings and to evaluate the accuracy of the displacement recovery technique.

This study examines the fluid dynamics of an array of droplets subjected to a sudden pressure impulse. We demonstrate that the interplay between the oscillatory and aperiodic components of the acoustic radiation force can be managed by adjusting the dimensionless parameters of the system. This interaction allows for precise tuning of the target droplet's displacement and velocity, as well as its net translation and drift.

The Internet of Things (IoT) has become a vital component of modern life, with IoT devices increasingly integrated into everyday activities. As these devices generate massive amounts of data, there is a growing demand for high-speed, low-latency, and reliable connectivity. Consequently, Quality of Service (QoS) has emerged as a critical factor for IoT applications, ensuring that users receive the necessary bandwidth, reliability, and low latency. This paper introduces a novel QoS framework designed for IoT environments, which leverages a hybrid approach combining supervised machine learning and deep reinforcement learning. The framework utilizes a deep Q-Network (DQN) to learn optimal actions for managing network resources, with a reward function that accounts for both device QoS and network performance. Additionally, the system employs a supervised machine learning model to predict network conditions, enabling the DQN to make informed decisions based on these forecasts. The proposed framework was evaluated using a simulated network environment, with results demonstrating its effectiveness in optimizing resource allocation and enhancing overall network performance.

We present ALMA observations of the protoplanetary disk surrounding the young star TW Hydrae, which exhibits a prominent gap at approximately 1.5 AU. This study offers the most comprehensive view of the disk's inner region to date, revealing a complex architecture characterized by a series of concentric rings and a central cavity. The rings display significant variations in their widths and inclinations, with the outermost ring showing a distinct inward tilt. The disk's inclination and position angle align with those of the central star, suggesting that the rings and the central cavity are sculpted by a single embedded planet. This finding is supported by the observation of a Keplerian rotation pattern in the CO gas, which indicates the presence of a planet with a mass of roughly 10 Jupiter masses ($10 M_{\rm Jup}$). Furthermore, the CO gas distribution is significantly asymmetric, with the gas concentrated on the side of the disk facing away from the observer. The authors propose that this asymmetry results from the planet's orbital motion, which causes the gas to accumulate on the downwind side of the disk.

This paper introduces a novel vector-valued distance metric for analyzing symmetric positive definite (SPD) matrices, offering a fresh geometric perspective on this space. Unlike conventional scalar-valued approaches, this formulation facilitates the straightforward computation of weighted means and enables efficient, closed-form solutions for regression and clustering tasks. The text further investigates the statistical properties of this distance and substantiates its validity through both synthetic experiments and real-world applications.

The hydrogen network is increasingly recognized as a flexible asset that can bolster the stability of electricity grids. By leveraging its capacity to store energy, it can mitigate fluctuations in renewable generation, thereby supporting a higher share of renewables within the power system. This study examines the synergistic interaction between electricity and hydrogen networks, specifically focusing on how the hydrogen network can smooth renewable energy variability. A model is developed to simulate the power flow across both systems, incorporating the hydrogen network's ability to absorb excess renewable energy for later use. The analysis evaluates the impact of varying the hydrogen network's charging speed on overall system flexibility. Results indicate that while slower charging rates enhance system balance, they may not be optimal for all scenarios, and a moderate charging rate can be more effective in certain contexts. Ultimately, the findings demonstrate that integrating the hydrogen network can substantially boost the penetration of renewable energy sources.

We introduce a novel technique for estimating the orientation of horizontal magnetic fields beneath the surface by analyzing travel time anisotropy derived from the travel times of S-waves. This approach is grounded in the observation that subsurface magnetic fields induce anisotropy in S-wave propagation, a phenomenon that can be quantified through the travel times of S-waves recorded by a seismic array. We validate this method using a synthetic dataset generated from a 3D finite-difference model of a heterogeneous medium with a defined magnetic field. The results demonstrate that the proposed method successfully recovers the true field orientation, achieving a standard deviation of 1.5° for the strike angle and 2.0° for the dip angle.

Squeezed light serves as a vital resource for quantum information processing and sensing, yet generating it in the extreme ultraviolet (XUV) spectrum remains a significant hurdle. This study demonstrates the creation of XUV squeezed states using a quantum-optical parametric amplifier situated within the high-harmonic generation region of an intense laser. By analyzing the pump depletion effect, the authors reveal that the parametric process is significantly more efficient when the pump laser operates at a frequency that supports the generation of the highest possible harmonics. This approach is further shown to be broadly applicable, capable of producing squeezed states across a wide spectrum of light sources.

This paper addresses the challenge of transporting a drone from an initial to a final waypoint within the shortest possible timeframe. We model the vehicle as a point subject to bounded acceleration, a standard representation for many quadcopters, and develop a control input that minimizes travel time. By applying Pontryagin's minimum principle, we derive the optimal solution, which consists of a constant-magnitude acceleration profile switching between two directions. Simulations confirm that this control strategy effectively reduces movement time, with the results validating the proposed approach.

This study examines the structure of additive conjugacy codes within the ring $\mathcal{R}=\mathbb{F}_{p^k}[x]/\langle x^r-g(x)\rangle$, where $g(x)$ is irreducible over $\mathbb{F}_{p^k}$ and $p^k$ is a prime. We demonstrate that the linear structure of the dual code for an $\mathcal{R}$-linear additive conjugacy code is equivalent to a linear cyclic code defined over $\mathbb{F}_{p^k}[\,x\,]/\langle x^r+h(x)\rangle$, where $h(x)$ is also an irreducible polynomial over $\mathbb{F}_{p^k}$. Additionally, we establish that an $\mathcal{R}$-linear additive conjugacy code can be generated by a $p^k$-constriuctive polynomial.

Physicists seeking employment face significant challenges, particularly when targeting primarily undergraduate institutions (PDs) and community colleges (CCs), which often lack sufficient funding and resources to attract qualified staff. This paper examines the recruitment and hiring experiences of physicists at these two types of institutions, identifying common obstacles and successful strategies. We conducted a survey targeting physicists actively pursuing roles at CCs and PDs, as well as those already employed there. The results reveal that while both groups face similar hurdles, CCs and recent hires report greater difficulties in securing and retaining talent. We also present

This paper investigates the eigenvalues associated with the signed adjacency matrices of power hypergraphs. We demonstrate that these eigenvalues can be derived from those of signed subgraphs, thereby enabling the application of established results from signed graphs to these structures. Furthermore, we establish connections between the spectra of power hypergraphs and those of their line hypergraphs, as well as their tensor expressions.

The upcoming era of satellites within mega-constellations will necessitate highly efficient communication and navigation frameworks. This paper introduces a new framework for cooperative localization among these satellites, leveraging the inter-satellite links (ISL) to enhance positioning accuracy. By utilizing a cooperative approach, each satellite can determine its position based on its own measurements and the data received from neighboring nodes. This method is highly advantageous for satellites in large constellations because it significantly reduces the dependency on ground stations. To address the inherent complexity of the localization problem, we propose a decentralized algorithm that employs a distributed consensus mechanism to facilitate inter-satellite data sharing. Theoretical analysis confirms the algorithm's convergence, while numerical simulations demonstrate its efficacy. Furthermore, we highlight the algorithm's potential to support various applications, including distributed formation control and distributed navigation.

We report the discovery of transit timing variations (TTVs) in the WASP-12 system, which exhibit a period of approximately 100 days. This finding suggests that the hot Jupiter WASP-12 b underwent orbital migration, likely driven by the presence of an additional, as yet undetected, planet. We modeled the TTV data using a two-planet configuration, which successfully accounts for the observed variations with an orbital period of roughly 100 days. The best-fit model indicates a companion planet with a mass of 0.13 ± 0.02 Jupiter masses and a semi-major axis of 0.19 ± 0.01 AU.

This study introduces a novel calibration approach for the 21-cm power spectrum, utilizing a 2-point correlation function between the 21-cm signal and the Ly$\alpha$ flux distribution. By employing a 2-point function, we can isolate the 21-cm signal's response to specific large-scale structures, thereby enhancing sensitivity to calibration errors and reducing systematic biases. Furthermore, we implement a machine learning-based method to determine the response function, which boosts the signal-to-noise ratio for detecting the 21-cm signal. This framework is applied to the Ly$\alpha$ field from the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) and the 21-cm data from the Murchison Widefield Array (MWA). Our analysis indicates that this technique can significantly improve the 21-cm power spectrum measurement, achieving a 21-cm signal-to-noise ratio of approximately 1000 for the DESI field and roughly 100 for the MWA data.

We demonstrate that if an algebraic GKM manifold $X$ possesses algebraically equivariant vector bundles $E$ and $F$ with identical equivariant Chern classes, then $E$ and $F$ are equivariantly isomorphic. This result extends beyond vector bundles to apply to algebraically equivariant coherent sheaves as well.
We present an elementary proof of prime number theorem that relies solely on Riemann's $\zeta$-function functional equation and elementary techniques.

Mixed models featuring categorical time are commonly employed in repeated-measures analyses of clinical trials. However, this approach necessitates estimating a separate intercept for each time point, which can lead to substantial loss of degrees of freedom and result in imprecise estimates. To address this, we introduce a novel method for modeling repeated-measures time as a continuous interval rather than a categorical variable. By utilizing a restricted cubic spline basis to represent time flexibly, our approach yields more accurate parameter estimates and greater statistical power compared to traditional methods. We demonstrate the efficacy of this proposed technique through a simulation study and an analysis of data from a clinical trial.

This paper introduces a crowdsourcing algorithm designed for connected vehicle routing, which leverages the vehicle-to-vehicle (V2V) communication capabilities of vehicles to share real-time traffic data. By utilizing this information, the algorithm recommends routes to vehicles based on their current locations and travel preferences. The study evaluates the algorithm's performance regarding travel time savings, the percentage of vehicles successfully finding routes, and the total number of route recommendations generated. Results indicate that the proposed algorithm outperforms existing methods in these metrics. Furthermore, it demonstrates that the algorithm's efficiency in generating recommendations and the total number of route opportunities increases with higher levels of vehicular connectivity.

It is widely recognized that neural networks possessing a landscape of flat minima tend to generalize better. This study introduces a new class of optimizers designed specifically to locate such minima, which we term "flat-minima optimizers." Our approach involves modifying the Hessian of the loss function within gradient descent steps, thereby steering the optimizer toward regions characterized by lower curvature. We demonstrate that our method surpasses existing first-order approximations in the Hessian, such as flatness-normalized SGD, and validates its effectiveness through experiments on image classification and regression tasks.

This paper introduces a new approach to mitigate electromagnetic interference (EMI) in wireless radios by utilizing compact, reflective diode-based parametric frequency selective limiters (FSLs). Unlike traditional absorbing FLSs, this reflective design offers a more straightforward implementation and superior selectivity. The proposed reflective FSL comprises a two-element resonator that leverages the nonlinear reactance of parametric diodes to create nonlinear filtering. The study provides a theoretical analysis of the nonlinear behavior of this resonator, supported by experimental results from a two-stage reflective FSL prototype. The results demonstrate that this reflective architecture can effectively attenuate unwanted signals while preserving the transmission of the desired radio frequency.

This study introduces a stochastic compartmental model designed to examine the transmission dynamics of infectious diseases, specifically tailored for the early stages of the COVID-19 outbreak in China. By incorporating stochastic elements into a standard deterministic framework, this paper explores the conditions under which an epidemic either vanishes or persists. Furthermore, it derives the expression for the basic reproduction number, $\mathcal{R}_0$, and establishes both a sufficient and a necessary condition for disease extinction versus sustained presence. The paper concludes with numerical simulations that validate the theoretical findings.

We present a straightforward, efficient, and effective method for creating vector representations of phrases, which extends existing approaches that only handle words. By leveraging the fact that phrases are essentially collections of words, our technique utilizes established word-level embedding models. We demonstrate that these vector representations achieve strong performance across multiple natural language processing tasks, including entity typing, machine reading comprehension, and text classification.

This paper examines the number of components of order $k$ within a random geometric graph, denoted as $X_{n,k}$, defined on a unit sphere. The vertices of such a graph are selected uniformly and independently at random, with edges existing between pairs of vertices whose distance does not exceed a fixed threshold $r$. We demonstrate that, as $n$ approaches infinity, the mean and variance of $X_{n,k}$ both scale as $O(n^0)$. Furthermore, we establish that the distribution of $X_{n,k}$ converges to a Poisson distribution with parameter $\lambda$, where $\lambda$ depends on the volume of the set of points on the unit sphere within a distance $r$ from a given point.

We introduce a new method for numerically solving the equilibrium configurations of rotating stars, grounded in a Lagrangian description of a self-gravitating, compressible fluid. This framework employs a novel set of independent variables that facilitate a direct and precise representation of arbitrary Lagrangian element trajectories. We demonstrate that this Lagrangian formulation is mathematically equivalent to the traditional Eulerian approach, confirming its validity. Furthermore, we outline a robust numerical scheme for solving the associated equations and present numerical results for both differentially and uniformly rotating stellar models.

This study investigates the generalized Lemaître-Tolman-Bondi spacetime, demonstrating that it shares fundamental characteristics with standard inhomogeneous LTB spacetime. Specifically, we examine the topology and geodesic completeness of the manifold, as well as its singularity structure. Furthermore, we analyze how these generalized solutions relate to black hole formation and cosmological models. The results indicate that the overall structural nature remains invariant; thus, generalized LTB spacetime can effectively serve as a framework for constructing realistic inhomogeneous cosmologies.

We demonstrate that a strongly nonlocal multipartile set of orthogonal quantum states can be constructed using two distinct approaches: the product states derived from a $2 \times 3$ Bell diagonal state and the product states generated by an unextendible entangled set. Furthermore, we establish that any strongly nonlocal collection of product states can be expanded into a larger set of product states that remains strongly nonlocal but lacks Bell-entanglement among its members. Finally, we prove that given any two strongly nonlocal sets of product states, one can be transformed into the other via local stochastic operations.

Web usage mining serves as a valuable resource for understanding user behavior, with the goal of understanding these users to enhance the web experience. A key area of study is "visit intention," which refers to the specific objective a user aims to achieve during a browsing session. This paper introduces a method for automatically identifying the intention behind web visits. The approach utilizes a taxonomy of web categories to construct a categorical sequence, which is then matched against a taxonomy of activity types to find the most similar one. This technique is evaluated using a dataset of 100,000 sessions from the University of Almeria's web logs. The results demonstrate that the method achieves an accuracy of 70.8%, indicating its effectiveness.

This paper investigates the performance of a transmissive reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-aided multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) system operating in a dual-functional mode where the RIS beamforming (BF) approach is designed to simultaneously enhance communication rates and generate free-space optical (FSO) links for sensing. The study analyzes the impact of various RIS configurations, including fixed and adaptable beamforming, on the system's communication and sensing capabilities. The findings demonstrate that the proposed dual-functional transmissive RIS (T-RIS) outperforms conventional single-functional counterparts, yielding a communication rate gain of 1.5 dB and an improved sensing accuracy of 1.5 times.

Offline reinforcement learning (RL) focuses on training policies using static datasets, yet most existing approaches are not designed for real-world deployment where new data accumulates over time. This paper addresses the critical gap in incremental learning for offline RL. We introduce a novel framework that facilitates policy improvement with limited incremental data, rigorously analyzing its theoretical properties and validating them through experiments on standard benchmarks.

We demonstrate free theorems applicable to polymorphic functions residing within reflexive objects, a concept that encompasses both untyped $\lambda$-calculi and strongly typed systems featuring unifiable types. This work extends previous findings by Wadler, where free theorems were derived specifically for uninhabited types.
