This paper introduces necessary optimality conditions for constrained mathematical programming problems set in locally convex spaces, utilizing the support function and the support of dual space elements as a dual variable representation. These conditions are derived through duality relationships between convex sets in primal locally convex spaces and convex sets in dual spaces. Finally, specific examples are provided to validate the correctness of these necessary optimality conditions.

We demonstrate that a specific D-brane configuration admits a near-horizon geometry that supports a supersymmetric vacuum. This solution, representing the type IIA supergravity solution for a stack of D2-D4-D6 bound states, exhibits an $AdS_4 \times S^5$ near-horizon structure and possesses a $U(1)^3$ isometry. Our analysis indicates that this vacuum is supersymmetric when the dimension parameter $d$ is odd; specifically, it serves as the $d=3$ instance of the $AdS_4 \times S^5$ vacuum.

We investigate the dynamics of a strongly-coupled gauge theory featuring a first-order thermal phase transition, utilizing holographic duality. Our analysis demonstrates that when phase domains collide at low velocities, they generate sound waves, confirming that the presence of a sound mode in the post-collision hydrodynamic flow can indicate the existence of a first-order phase transition. Additionally, we observe that domain walls annihilate more slowly in systems with higher viscosity, and that collision outcomes are significantly influenced by the presence of black hole horizon structures.

While deep reinforcement learning (DRL) has recently excelled in robotics, it often demands extensive training and suffers from poor sample efficiency. Conversely, traditional control methods are sample-efficient but struggle with complex tasks. This paper introduces Bayesian Controller Fusion (BCF), a new approach that combines the sample efficiency of classical control with the adaptability of DRL. BCF operates by integrating a learned, parameterized DRL policy into a parametric controller, treating the policy as a prior distribution over control parameters. This framework enables the system to adapt to new environments by updating the posterior distribution of parameters based on observed rewards. We demonstrate that BCF can be implemented using standard Bayesian inference techniques, such as particle filters, and we provide theoretical analysis regarding the convergence of these posteriors. Extensive experiments on simulated and real-world hardware involving locomotion and manipulation tasks show that BCF outperforms both standard DRL and traditional control methods.

Acute ischemic stroke (AIS) is a critical emergency characterized by a sudden blockage of cerebral blood flow, resulting in severe neurological deficits. In clinical practice, perfusion imaging is employed to identify distinct tissue areas within the brain, specifically the penumbra and core, which are widely recognized as the "saver" and "sacrificial zones," respectively. This study introduces a novel deep learning framework designed to segment these perfusion regions using a single CT perfusion map. The approach utilizes a U-Net architecture enhanced with a new attention mechanism to generate precise segmentation masks. Furthermore, the framework incorporates a dedicated post-processing module to refine the accuracy of the segmentation. Experimental results demonstrate that the model achieves a Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC) of 0.79, with a 95% confidence interval of 074 to 084, and a sensitivity of 071 (95% CI: 066 to 076). These findings indicate that the proposed method offers a robust and reliable solution for clinical applications.

Zero-jettiness beam functions, which link the factorization of soft and collinear operators in the denominator of a cross section to the numerator, are vital for high-precision calculations in collider physics. This study derives the complete analytic one-loop form of these functions, including finite terms, for quark-antiquark fusion into any final state. We demonstrate that this result is consistent with prior findings by Belin, Boussarie, and de Florian, which were presented solely in a form suitable for integration. Furthermore, we provide a numerical comparison of the two approaches.

A graph is defined as chordal if it contains no induced cycles of length four or greater. This paper presents a polynomial-time algorithm for recognizing chordal graphs, which also outputs a triangulation of a given graph within the chordal class.

This study introduces a novel approach to sound source separation that utilizes multiple semantic concepts. By employing a deep neural network to simultaneously predict several concept labels, we enable the model to leverage inter-relationships between these concepts for improved separation performance. The method is evaluated on the Soundtrack separation dataset, where the concepts denote the musical instruments present in the audio. Experimental results indicate that our approach outperforms existing methods, with further improvements observed when combining multiple concept categories.

We investigate the concept of block coherence, defined as the minimal sum of diagonal entries across all possible block-diagonal unitary transformations of a given quantum state. Our study demonstrates that this metric offers a quantitative benchmark for the usefulness of quantum states in parameter estimation tasks. Furthermore, we examine the relationship between block coherence and coherence, noting that while block coherence provides a lower bound for estimation usefulness, it does so in a way that is suboptimal compared to standard coherence measures.

We report a comprehensive study of the X-ray variability and timing characteristics of the black hole binary H 1743-322 during its 2018–2019 outbursts, utilizing data from the Swift-XRT and NuSTAR instruments. The observations span a wide range of spectral states, from the hard to the soft state. We employed a Bayesian framework to determine the fractional root-mean-square (rms) amplitude and coherence of quasi-periodic oscillations (QPOs) and their associated power spectra. The fractional rms of the QPOs exhibits a strong anti-correlation with the non-thermal fraction of the emission, a relationship that persists across all observed outbursts. We also investigated the power spectral density (PSD) of the source, finding that the PSDs of the soft-state outbursts display a "broken" power-law structure, whereas the hard-state outbursts show a "double-horned" profile. This paper details our methodology for participating in the second challenge of the COVID-19 Open Research Dataset Challenge, which focused on conducting an open research analysis of COVID-19. Our approach involved applying natural language processing techniques to answer specific research questions derived from the dataset.

We present a new, self-consistent, and self-regulating framework for the thermal evolution of the Warm Hot Intergalactic Medium (WHIM). This model incorporates galactic outflows and accretion shocks, which are recognized as primary heating mechanisms for the WHIM. By integrating these processes, the model achieves a more accurate representation of the thermal structure of the intergalactic medium (IGM) and better aligns with observational data. Specifically, the model successfully reproduces the observed correlation between the temperature and density of the IGM, as well as the relationship between the temperature and density of the WHIM. Furthermore, the model predicts a more realistic distribution of the WHIM's temperature and density, which is consistent with recent observations. This framework provides a more robust basis for understanding the thermal evolution of the WHIM and its implications for the evolution of the universe.

We introduce a new randomized algorithm capable of identifying a leftmost separator of size no greater than $k$ with a success probability of at least $1 - 1/n^c$ in $O(n^2 \log^2 n)$ time, where $n$ represents the number of vertices and $c$ is a constant. This approach is highly effective for applications involving the sequential processing of multiple queries.

Tidal Disruption Events (TDEs) are hypothesized to occur when stars approach too closely to supermassive black holes (SMBHs), a phenomenon that could serve as a novel method for classifying galaxies. This study examines the feasibility of using TDEs to distinguish between galaxies hosting active and inactive SMBHs, as well as those residing in dark matter halos. We simulated the orbits of stars within galaxies of varying morphologies and sizes, incorporating diverse dark matter halo profiles, and tracked the resulting outcomes. Our results indicate that TDEs are more probable in galaxies situated within massive dark matter halos, suggesting that TDEs could effectively identify such systems. Additionally, we analyzed the relationship between the luminosity of TDEs and the mass of the central SMBHs, finding that TDEs originating in galaxies with massive halos tend to exhibit higher luminosities.

Reconfigurable Wireless Networks (RWNs) are designed to support applications with demanding Quality of Service (QoS) requirements by utilizing reconfigurable antennas. These networks can dynamically adjust radiation patterns to optimize performance and support diverse services. However, the vast number of possible radiation patterns creates a combinatorial explosion, making it difficult to identify the optimal configuration for a specific scenario. To address this challenge, we introduce a multi-agent reinforcement learning framework that learns optimal patterns through interaction with the environment. In this approach, a central agent selects the most suitable pattern for a specific reconfigurable user based on their current state, while auxiliary agents refine the action space to accelerate learning. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this method through simulation results.

This paper introduces a new approach termed "extended word alignment," which expands the traditional alignment between baseform and inflected forms. The goal is to enhance the efficiency of human post-editing by enabling the correction of errors on entire sequences of words through a single operation. We demonstrate that this expansion significantly improves the alignment accuracy of baseline systems. Furthermore, we validate the system's utility through controlled experiments with human annotators, which confirm that the approach substantially boosts post-editor productivity.

In recent years, the study of rotating black holes within modified gravity frameworks has gained significant attention. This work examines the Kerr-like rotating black hole solution within a specific $f(R,T)$ gravity model, focusing on the physical implications of the spacetime's physical quantities. Furthermore, the analysis investigates the thermodynamic properties of this black hole, specifically its stability, within a heat bath environment.

Numerical simulations of astrophysical phenomena frequently exhibit cylindrical symmetry, offering a chance to capitalize on this trait to boost computational efficiency. This paper introduces a novel method for implementing such symmetry within the context of Arbitrary Lagrangian-Eulerian (ALE) grid frameworks. Our approach involves two primary steps: first, we map the physical domain from cylindrical to one-dimensional ALE coordinates, and subsequently, we apply a staggered, high-order scheme featuring central differencing for staggered variables and one-sided biased stencils for forward/backward extrapolation. We demonstrate the method's accuracy through numerical experiments involving both steady-state and time-dependent scenarios. Furthermore, we validate its performance in astrophysical applications, specifically by modeling the post-merger evolution of binary neutron stars.

This study reports the investigation of $D^{(*)+}_{sJ}$ mesons produced in $B^+ \to D^{(*)+}_{sJ} K^- K^0_{\rm S}$ decays, utilizing a data sample of $1.0 \times 10^8$ $B^+$ mesons collected by the BESIII detector at a center-of-mass energy of 4.6 GeV. The $D^+_{sJ}$ candidates are identified through their decays into $K^+ \pi^-$. The analysis reveals two distinct peaks within the $D^{(*)+}_{sJ}$ invariant mass spectrum, located at approximately 2.47 GeV and 2.55 GeV, respectively. The resonance at 2.47 GeV is identified as the $D^+_{sJ}(2460)$, while the peak at 2.55 GeV is assigned to the $D^+_{s1}(2536)$. The measured branching fractions for the decay $B^+ \to D^+_{s1}(2536) K^- K^0_{\rm S}$ and $B^+ \to D^+_{s1}(2536) K^- K^- K^0_{\rm S}$ are determined to be $(1.09 \pm 0.12) \times

This paper investigates the approximation properties of fractal polynomials defined on the Sierpi\`ski Gasket (SG). Initially, we establish the existence of fractal polynomials of any given order $n$ that approximate the continuous function space on the SG within an $\epsilon$-neighborhood. Subsequently, we demonstrate that for any $n$, there exists a unique polynomial of that degree which minimizes this approximation error. Finally, we provide the construction necessary to identify this optimal polynomial explicitly.

This study introduces Guided Visual Question Generation (GVQG), a new task designed to create questions from images by incorporating additional textual guidance. We define two specific scenarios: Guided Visual Question Generation with a Suggested Topic (GVQG-T) and GVQG without a Suggested Topic (GVQG-O). For these tasks, we present the GVID dataset, which includes images alongside user-defined prompts. We also develop GVQG-Zero, a novel zero-shot approach for this domain. Empirical results indicate that our method significantly surpasses existing state-of-the-art techniques, producing questions that are more closely aligned with the provided textual hints.

The formation of dark matter cores in dwarf galaxies is widely attributed to supernova (SN) feedback, where the energy injected into the halo is hypothesized to be sufficient to create these cores. This study examines the relationship between the SN energy injection rate and the extent of core formation. We demonstrate that the maximum size of the core is primarily determined by the rate at which energy is injected into the dark matter halo. Specifically, a higher injection rate results in a larger core. Furthermore, we establish a lower threshold for the energy injection rate required to form a dark matter core.

This paper introduces a straightforward method for converting higher-order logic into propositional form, which serves as a precursor to various propositional optimization strategies. This approach is implemented within the higher-order extension of the Coq proof assistant, named HOL-Coq. The technique is designed to be universally applicable to any higher-order theory, regardless of the specific syntax or semantics employed by the logic. Its primary objective is to facilitate the application of existing propositional processing methods, such as simplification, thereby enabling their use in higher-order reasoning. The authors illustrate this technique by demonstrating how to apply standard tools for propositional simplification and satisfiability within HOL-Coq.

In zero-sum games, replicator dynamics can generate limit cycles characterized by rotational oscillations around the unique interior equilibrium. These movements are driven by the persistent dominance of alternative strategies, which continuously shift as a result. The current study introduces a novel class of zero-sum games, defined by their limit cycles' ability to encompass the interior equilibrium within the polygon representing the dynamically stable strategy set.

We demonstrate that, under mild conditions, the pointwise estimate of a given point follows a normal distribution, converging to a Gaussian limit with a variance determined by a specific, explicit formula. We further derive the uniform distributional properties of the random forest estimator, establishing conditions under which it converges to a Gaussian process. We provide the covariance function for this limiting process and show that it is continuous, thus confirming the existence of a Gaussian random forest process. This study examines the collective charging and discharging of electric vehicles (EVs) within a distribution network. The proposed approach utilizes a game-theoretic framework to align individual EV optimization with grid voltage support. By integrating a voltage support component into the EV power control, the method aims to alleviate voltage stress. The analysis demonstrates that coordinating this control across a fleet of EVs enhances grid voltages and averts voltage violations. This study presents a comprehensive investigation into the structural and magnetic characteristics of single crystals of SmFeO₃, synthesized via the floating zone method. The findings indicate that the orthorhombic structure of SmFeO₃ is stabilized by the lanthanide contraction effect, which intensifies as the ionic radius of the rare-earth cation decreases. This trend correlates with a corresponding increase in the magnetic ordering temperature. Furthermore, the research highlights the material's potential for applications in spintronics and magneto-optoelectronics, specifically noting that SmFeO₃ exhibits a large magnetocaloric effect.

Ecologists have long utilized the concept of "niche" to describe the functional roles populations play within ecosystems. This study introduces a fresh perspective on this idea, framing it as the set of capabilities required for a population to persist and exert influence over its surroundings. We demonstrate that this definition encompasses the entire spatial and temporal history of a population, including its past existence. Furthermore, we establish that a population's niche is intrinsically linked to its extinction risk and its potential to displace other species. These findings offer a new framework for understanding how species occupy ecological spaces and how such populations evolve over time.

This study introduces a black-box modeling approach for developing model predictive control (MPC) frameworks to manage ventilation in buildings, specifically designed to function with limited datasets. The methodology utilizes a deep neural network to model the system dynamics, which is subsequently integrated into an MPC structure. The paper details the training process using simulated data and outlines an implementation strategy for real-world deployment. The proposed method is validated through numerical experiments, demonstrating its ability to regulate indoor air quality and minimize energy consumption.

We report the discovery of a hydrogen-poor superluminous supernova (SLSN) designated as AT2020fyc, which exhibits a luminosity of $M_{r}=-19.6$ mag at peak brightness. Its spectral characteristics and light-curve evolution closely resemble those of SN 2015L. By analyzing the spectral data, we determined that the progenitor star had a mass of approximately $15\,M_{\odot}$, and the explosion was driven by the interaction between the ejecta and a dense, slow-moving circumstellar medium (CSM). This interaction mechanism is further supported by the observed rapid decline in the supernova's luminosity.

Theoretical predictions suggest that 2D magnets exhibit a hysteresis landscape fundamentally distinct from their 3D counterparts. This study investigates the experimental verification of such a 2D limit by examining the magnetic hysteresis of Cr$_2$Ge$_2$Te$_6$ (a van der Waals ferromagnet) across varying thicknesses. We observed that the magnetization reversal mechanism shifts from a 3D-like behavior in bulk samples to a 2D-like mechanism in monolayers, a transition confirmed by the scaling of the coercive field with thickness. Furthermore, we identified a scaling relationship between the coercive field and the inverse square root of the sample area, a hallmark of 3D magnetism. In contrast, the two-dimensional limit is defined by a scaling of the coercive field with the inverse square root of the thickness. These findings offer a pathway to engineer the hysteresis properties of van der Waals magnets by precisely controlling their geometric dimensions.

The quality of training data is crucial for the success of machine learning applications. This study investigates how word concreteness influences the acquisition of dependency grammars. We demonstrate that incorporating words with higher concreteness values into training datasets significantly enhances the performance of the acquired grammars. Furthermore, we introduce a method for refining dependency grammars by eliminating abstract terms through substitution with their more concrete counterparts. The results indicate that grammars developed from datasets enriched with this process exhibit a greater capacity for parsing novel sentences.

We introduce a novel evaluation framework for assessing the importance of pixels in predictions generated by image models. This framework is founded on a new metric called the "pixel score," which represents the magnitude of the gradient of the prediction with respect to the input pixel values. We demonstrate that this metric is highly effective for analyzing how pixels contribute to these predictions.

This study examines a reflection-symmetric thin-shell wormhole featuring a non-symmetric geometry. It is established that this model possesses a singularity-free event horizon, serving as an ideal framework for investigating the behavior of light rays. We analyze the optical characteristics of this structure by examining the characteristics of geodesic paths and the specific conditions under which these paths become trapped. Furthermore, we determine the specific conditions required for an observer to witness a "photon sphere," a phenomenon typically associated with black holes.

We present a fresh functional inequality that serves as a novel counterpart to the Bakry-\'Emery-Ledoux inequality. This tool enables us to demonstrate the existence of a uniform spectral gap across a range of multi-particle collision models, encompassing both hard and soft interactions.

We introduce a novel method for analyzing the trimer cover configurations of an infinite square lattice, a technique that relies on the application of the transfer matrix method to a finite rectangular grid with an imposed width constraint. By deriving exact expressions for trimer cover densities on a rectangular lattice, we employ these results to determine the asymptotic behavior of trimer cover densities on an infinite square lattice.

Reconstructing a 3D object from a single 2D image is a challenging task, particularly when the viewpoint is unrecognizable. This difficulty stems from the inherent information loss during 2D projection, which can be mitigated by integrating prior object knowledge. This paper proposes a method for inferring 3D object structure from a single 2D input by leveraging a pre-trained 3D object prior. Our approach utilizes a latent 3D representation to predict the camera's pose and the object's appearance, which are then combined to generate the final 2D output. By training this prior on a vast dataset of 3D objects, we enable the model to infer a latent 3D shape that aligns with the input image. This mechanism effectively captures the 3D structure, which can also be employed for tasks such as 3D shape completion. We validate our method's efficacy through comparisons with state-of-the-art techniques on the ShapeNet dataset.

Query Graph Ranking (QGR) involves ranking knowledge graph entities based on a natural language query. While neural network-based approaches have achieved high accuracy, they struggle with three primary challenges: (1) handling complex query structures that contain multiple sub-questions, (2) interpreting the query's semantic intent, and (3) selecting the appropriate knowledge graph relations. To address these issues, we introduce a novel framework called Relation-to-Path Ranking (R2PR). This approach first decomposes complex queries into multiple sub-questions, ranks candidate entities for each sub-question, and finally aggregates the results to determine the final ranking. The core of R2PR is a novel query decomposition mechanism that leverages the query's semantic intent to split it into a sequence of sub-questions. This decomposition is executed by a decomposition model that utilizes a query-semantic attention mechanism to identify the query's intent. Additionally, a ranking model is designed to select relevant knowledge graph relations for each sub-question and rank entities accordingly. Experimental results on two public datasets demonstrate that R2PR outperforms existing methods.

This paper introduces the concept of polynomial composites, extending algebraic notions of function composition to polynomials with coefficients in a commutative ring. We examine fundamental algebraic characteristics of polynomial composition, including associativity, and detail various algebraic structures derived from this operation, such as subalgebras and ideals. Furthermore, we explore the implications of these structures for the study of polynomial composition. Finally, we present a novel class of polynomials that exhibit specific properties relevant to polynomial composition, which we believe could prove valuable in broader applications.

Named Entity Disambiguation (NED) involves identifying the correct Wikipedia entity for a specific mention, a task that remains difficult due to the scarcity of training data and the frequent occurrence of ambiguous entities. This paper introduces a novel approach that leverages the rich semantic information within Wikipedia to enhance NED performance. Specifically, we propose a new feature set derived from the entities' corresponding Wikipedia infoboxes, which are then utilized to train a classifier. Our experiments demonstrate that this method outperforms existing state-of-the-art techniques.

This paper calculates the one-loop oblique parameters within the Minimal Supersymmetric Standard Model (MSSM) using the basis of mass eigenstates. Explicit formulas detailing the one-loop contributions to $S$, $W$, and $\Delta\alpha$ are presented, along with a brief discussion of their behavior in various limits.

We introduce a method for synthesizing new viewpoints from monocular footage of dynamic scenes. Our approach utilizes a recurrently trained neural network that generates novel views by integrating the input video with an initial reference image. This model is trained on a dataset of 3D dynamic scene reconstructions derived from video, enabling it to predict 3D pixel displacements and color values for target camera positions. Consequently, new views can be synthesized by combining these predicted attributes with corresponding textures from the source video. Experiments conducted on both synthetic and real-world datasets demonstrate that our technique achieves superior performance compared to existing methods.

This study examines a rough differential equation featuring a drift term that exhibits damping and is characterized as rough. We analyze the asymptotic behavior of the associated linearized flow. Specifically, we demonstrate that within a suitable function space, this flow forms a contraction mapping.

This research examines a grain model with long-range dependence defined over a Poisson process featuring a non-stationary intensity that scales according to a power law with the parameter $H$, where $0 < H < 1$. The random grain structure itself is governed by a scaling parameter $H$ within the interval $(0, 1)$. We demonstrate that the resulting random measure exhibits a second-order structure characterized by long-range dependence.

Reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RISs) are anticipated to be a foundational technology in emerging 6G wireless systems. This study investigates the joint design of RIS phase shifts and multi-user power allocation within a RIS-assisted multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) downlink framework. The primary objective is to maximize the minimum energy efficiency (EE) across all users, subject to RIS element phase constraints and limits on the total transmit power. To address this, we initially transform the original non-convex EE maximization problem into an equivalent form constrained by a minimum throughput requirement. Subsequently, we introduce an iterative algorithm based on block coordinate descent (BCD) to resolve the resulting problem. In each iteration, we derive a closed-form expression for optimal power allocation and develop a novel alternating least squares (ALS) method to calculate optimal phase shifts. The proposed ALS approach is further enhanced by introducing a new auxiliary variable to boost convergence speed. Simulation outcomes confirm that the EE performance of the devised algorithm surpasses that of benchmark solutions, while the overall computational complexity remains significantly lower than existing methods.

This study addresses the problem of estimating the probability of rare events within a multi-agent stochastic framework. We introduce a new approach that leverages large deviation theory to derive a bound for the probability of such events, thereby pinpointing a low-occurrence region. Subsequently, we develop a Bayesian inference algorithm designed to operate under uncertainty and efficiently identify the smallest region encompassed by this probability bound. The efficacy of our proposed method is demonstrated through numerical simulations.

Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) are widely utilized for image classification, yet their computational demands often hinder deployment on resource-constrained devices. To address this, quantization offers a viable solution by reducing the precision of weights and activations, thereby lowering computational costs. However, this approach risks degrading accuracy. To counteract such losses, we introduce a novel quantization strategy that leverages the inherent sparsity of CNN weights. By applying a threshold to filter out negligible values, the method reduces the data size and accelerates inference. Furthermore, we propose a specific algorithm for optimizing the quantization bit-width, which is designed to maximize accuracy while maintaining a fixed memory budget. Experimental results on the ImageNet dataset demonstrate that the proposed algorithm effectively balances memory efficiency and model performance.

We present a novel mechanism for Type Ia supernovae that relies on the ignition of a white dwarf via a self-excited, positive feedback loop triggered by magnetic buoyancy. This process occurs when a magnetic field within a white dwarf destabilizes, breaches the stellar surface, and generates a magnetic flux tube. The resulting tube rises buoyantly, exerting magnetic pressure that compresses the underlying white dwarf and elevates its central temperature to the point of ignition. We demonstrate that this scenario is physically feasible for a white dwarf with a mass of 1.1 solar masses and a magnetic field strength of 10^10 Gauss. Furthermore, we illustrate that the parameters of the resulting supernova align with observational data.

This study examines online learning within deep nonlinear architectures, specifically addressing the allocation of limited computational resources (such as gradient descent steps) across network layers. We introduce a straightforward yet principled allocation strategy that prioritizes gradient descent steps for initial layers. This approach stems from the observation that initial layers capture input data features, which are critical for downstream computations. Our findings indicate that this method enhances performance in both supervised and unsupervised tasks. Furthermore, we demonstrate that this allocation scheme aligns with the theoretical analysis of online learning using two-layer neural networks.

The global spread of the SARS-CoV-2 virus has necessitated the urgent development of vaccines, yet the widespread availability of these vaccines is expected to be a prolonged process. Consequently, it is vital to maximize the efficient use of vaccines to achieve the highest possible impact. Blockchain technology offers a framework for creating decentralized applications (dApps) that can enhance efficiency and transparency in the healthcare sector. This paper introduces a blockchain-based application designed to facilitate the scheduling of COVID-19 tests and vaccinations. By enabling individuals to book appointments via a mobile interface, the system allows test results and vaccination records to be shared instantly with medical professionals. Additionally, the system incorporates a privacy-preserving mechanism that enables users to share their medical data with authorized doctors without revealing their personal identities. The application is built on the Ethereum blockchain using the Solidity smart contract language and the Truffle toolkit.

This study evaluates the efficacy of pre-trained sentence embedding models for text classification. We examine how various models perform across three classification tasks: sentiment analysis, hate speech detection, and text simplification. Our findings indicate that these sentence embeddings can effectively enhance classification performance.

We investigate the diffusion of quantum particles within a $d$-dimensional lattice subjected to a uniform magnetic field, specifically focusing on the impact of breaking particle-hole symmetry. Our analysis demonstrates that removing this symmetry induces a drift in the particle diffusion process. Furthermore, we examine the specific scenario where the drift velocity is nullified, revealing that the resulting diffusion coefficient exhibits divergence at critical points.

Kerr polarimetry serves as a sensitive tool for investigating the dynamics of quantum Hall ferromagnets. This study examines the decay of Kerr precession in the quantum Hall regime, revealing that its attenuation is governed by the specific ground state. In the absence of an inversion symmetry-breaking Zeeman field, the decay follows a power law, whereas a substantial Zeeman field induces exponential damping. We attribute this exponential attenuation to the precession's generation of a net spin current, which is subsequently scattered by edge states. Furthermore, we provide a closed-form analytical expression for the damping rate applicable to the large Zeeman field limit.

We investigate the dynamics of a conformal field theory under periodic driving, utilizing the holographic framework of AdS$_2$ gravity. Our analysis demonstrates that the system's behavior is captured by the dynamics of an effective cosmological constant within this gravitational model. We identify two distinct phases: a time-crystalline phase, defined by a negative effective cosmological constant, and a phase exhibiting a positive effective cosmological constant, which manifests as a black hole. We further examine the phase diagram of the effective cosmological constant and the corresponding properties of the associated black hole.

This paper introduces a new multimodal generative model designed for image-based depth estimation and motion forecasting. The system accepts RGB images as input and produces a joint probability distribution over depth and future frames. By training this model on a large-scale dataset of paired RGB images and inertial sensor data, we demonstrate that it surpasses current state-of-the-art methods in both depth estimation and motion forecasting tasks. Additionally, we apply the model to a robotic navigation scenario, proving its effectiveness in predicting future states to enhance the robustness of SLAM systems.

A measurement of the mixing-induced $C\!P$-violating phase $\phi_s$ in the decay channel $B_s^0 \to J/\psi \phi$ is reported using 9 fb$^{-1}$ of proton-proton collision data acquired by the LHCb detector at a center-of-mass energy of 7 TeV. The obtained value, $\phi_s = -0.029 \pm 0.022\,(\text{stat}) \pm 0.017\,( \text{sys})$ rad, aligns with the Standard Model prediction.

This study introduces a novel class of distributed optimal control strategies for linear time-invariant systems, termed Graph Symmetric Systems (GSSs). These systems are defined by specific graph structures and associated dynamic equations that exhibit particular symmetry properties. We present a fully distributed algorithm for GSSs that ensures convergence to the exact solution of the corresponding centralized optimal control problem. The algorithm operates by exchanging information exclusively with immediate neighbors, requiring only local knowledge of the system matrices, network topology, and individual agent states. Our approach is validated through numerical simulations demonstrating its effectiveness.

This paper introduces a truncation criterion designed for LMB-RFSet filters, aimed at managing filter complexity. The method effectively balances computational cost against performance by regulating the count of predicted components exceeding a defined threshold. Theoretical analysis demonstrates that this criterion can be established as Markovian, ensuring the existence of a time-average filter solution. Furthermore, an efficient implementation is developed, and simulation results confirm its effectiveness in managing complexity while maintaining accuracy.

A significant limitation of typological knowledge bases, such as the World Atlas of Language Structures (WATLS), is their susceptibility to bias, which undermines the utility of their data for linguistic research and computational linguistic studies. This study introduces a novel approach to mitigating such bias in typological databases by integrating information from comparable languages within the same family. We present and validate a semi-automated pipeline designed to identify these related languages, applying the method to WATLS to assess its effectiveness in reducing bias. Our findings demonstrate that this proposed strategy substantially decreases typological bias, thereby enhancing the overall quality of the database.

Off-policy evaluation (OPE) is a critical task in reinforcement learning (RL) that involves estimating the quality of a policy using only past interactions with the environment. This is especially vital for RL applications in high-stakes fields like healthcare and finance, where deploying a new policy before its evaluation is too risky. While recent research has focused on improving OPE performance, these approaches often rely on the assumption that the available data comes from a single, static environment. In reality, data frequently originates from multiple sources with varying environmental dynamics, such as different hospitals or regions. This paper introduces a new framework for OPE across a collection of environments with varying dynamics. We propose a new algorithm that leverages data from these diverse settings to achieve more accurate OPE. Theoretically, we establish the minimax lower bound for this problem and demonstrate that our method achieves an optimal convergence rate. Empirically, we show that our approach outperforms existing methods on both synthetic and real-world datasets.

Biopharmaceutical manufacturing relies on a lengthy fermentation process, which is highly susceptible to variations in raw materials and other unpredictable factors. To mitigate this, manufacturers employ a model designed to forecast the fermentation trajectory, enabling early detection of deviations and corrective actions. However, model inaccuracies can lead to flawed decisions, potentially causing the entire process to fail. Consequently, assessing model risk is critical for implementing effective risk mitigation strategies. This study introduces a Bayesian framework for quantifying model risk in fermentation, utilizing a Gaussian process to represent the stochastic nature of the process. The approach estimates the probability of model failure, defined as the likelihood that the model's predictions diverge significantly from the actual process behavior. We evaluated this methodology using a standard industrial fermentation model, applying it to a case study involving a biopharmaceutical production run.

This study examines the momentum-dependent contribution of the leading-order term in the strong-coupling expansion for the large polaron's energy-momentum relationship, as well as its corresponding effective mass. By employing a generalized variational approach that incorporates momentum, we derive an energy-momentum relation featuring a momentum-independent term at strong coupling, which aligns precisely with prior literature. Furthermore, we obtain an effective mass term that demonstrates a momentum dependency, a result that diverges from previous studies that assumed a momentum-independent mass.

We investigate the time evolution of the electric field operator at a single spatial point within a strong, uniform magnetic field. We demonstrate that the operator's correlation duration scales as a power law governed by the magnitude of the magnetic field, indicating an extended field lifetime under intense field conditions.

Quantum complementarity asserts that specific properties of a quantum system cannot be simultaneously defined. While the original concept of complementarity was formulated by N. Bohr, the complementary relation has been mathematically quantified by a number of authors. In this study, we examine a specific relation derived by S. Haroche regarding the field's phase and amplitude. We demonstrate that this relation adheres to a generalized form of complementarity, which accommodates a broader class of conjugate variables than the traditional formulation. Furthermore, we establish a generalized complementarity relation for the amplitude and phase within a coherent state.

We establish that counts of periodic arrangements avoiding a specific finite set of forbidden patterns along nonexpansive lines in two dimensions are inherently quantifiable by a finite collection of rational numbers.

The Borsuk number of a bounded metric space represents the minimum number of subsets required to partition the space such that each resulting sub-space has a strictly smaller diameter. This research examines the Borsuk number within the context of metric products, specifically analyzing cases where the Projections of the original set into the component metrics are either disjoint or cover the entirety of those component metrics.

We investigate a fourth-order operator defined on a subset of $\mathbb{R}^n$, which exhibits a singularity along a submanifold of codimension one. The primary objective is to construct an approximation for the operator's resolvent involving small positive parameters, accurate up to an exponentially decaying error term.

Training virtual assistants for low-resource languages presents significant challenges due to a scarcity of training data. This study introduces a new approach to generate synthetic data for these languages by leveraging transfer learning from high-resource counterparts. We introduce a method that utilizes a high-resource question-answer model to create synthetic question-answer pairs for a target language through translation. We evaluate this approach on the Amazon Alexa dataset, utilizing English as the high-resource source and German, Dutch, and Italian as the target languages. Our results indicate that the synthesized data yields performance improvements over a baseline model that relies on zero training samples.

This abstract details the design and implementation of SMT-Solve, an open-source API-based toolkit for solving Satisfiability Modulo Theories. The system is built upon Z3's C++ interface and provides a unified, user-friendly entry point for formulating and resolving problems across various logical theories. The core capabilities encompass theory unification, the integration of theories within satisfiability checks, and the extraction of specific model values. The paper also details the toolkit's construction, including the handling of complex logic combinations and the extraction of detailed proof proofs for unsatisfiable instances.

The study examines the quasi-exactly solvable (QES) states of a one-dimensional particle, defined as combinations of finite sums of harmonic oscillator states. We demonstrate that these QES states can be generated by applying a finite-dimensional ideal of a Lie algebra to the ground harmonic oscillator state. Furthermore, we derive a general formula for calculating the matrix elements of the harmonic oscillator states within the basis of these QES states.

This study investigates the link between input image resolution and the performance of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs). We introduce a novel methodology that enables the efficient assessment of how varying input resolutions affect CNN accuracy. Our approach involves generating a series of images at different resolutions from a single source and evaluating the target CNN's performance on this set. We apply this method to the popular ResNet-50 architecture, testing it on the ImageNet benchmark and various datasets from the COCO suite. Our findings indicate that higher input resolutions generally improve accuracy, but the rate of this improvement varies significantly depending on the dataset. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the method is versatile, capable of evaluating not only different CNN models but also distinct training protocols.

Binary asteroid systems are prime targets for future missions, such as the upcoming Double Asteroid Redirection Test mission, which will attempt to deflect a binary asteroid. To ensure mission success, it is critical to understand the physical characteristics of these systems, including their binary orbits and the effects of surface regolith. This study examines the spin dynamics of binary asteroid systems, specifically focusing on the influence of excited spin states on satellite surfaces. We demonstrate that such excited states can induce significant surface heating, potentially reaching temperatures of 100 K. This thermal energy may cause the regolith to sublimate, creating a localized plume of vapor and dust that exerts a force on the satellite. We calculate this force and compare it to the Yarkovsky and Yarkovsky-O'Keefe-Radzievskii-Paddack (YORP) effects. Our analysis indicates that for binary asteroid systems, the force generated by this regolith outgassing is comparable to, or even greater than, those caused by thermal radiation forces.

This paper investigates the horizon regularity of a scalar field within a black hole context, specifically examining the asymptotic behavior of the field near the horizon. We derive the regularity requirements that the scalar field must satisfy at the event horizon and utilize these conditions to formulate a boundary condition. Furthermore, we apply this condition to compute the reflection coefficient for scalar fields interacting with a Schwarzschild black hole.

This paper introduces a self-supervised framework for image denoising that utilizes a single noisy image as input, eliminating the need for paired clean-noisy data. The approach employs a dual-stream architecture: one branch processes the noisy image, while the other handles a synthetic clean image generated via a GAN. These streams are trained using a self-supervised loss function that leverages the degradation model to synthesize the expected clean output. The method's efficacy is validated through experiments on both real-world and synthetic noisy datasets, with comparative analyses against supervised and self-supervised baselines. Results indicate that the proposed method achieves superior performance compared to the supervised approach and performs on par with the self-supervised baseline.

This study addresses the k-sparse recovery problem, where the objective is to reconstruct a k-sparse vector x from measurements y = Ax. The authors introduce a novel algorithm named the "k-sparse" method, which is a streamlined variant of the "k-NN" algorithm. The k-sparse approach achieves superior performance in terms of both accuracy and speed compared to k-NN. Furthermore, the paper demonstrates that the computational complexity of the k-sparse method is significantly lower than that of the k-NN approach.

Union and intersection types are essential features in gradually typed environments like TypeScript, yet their verification remains computationally demanding. To address this, we introduce a novel, efficient approach for evaluating these types within the gradually typed calculus proposed by Sankin et al. (2018). Our method leverages a novel, compact, and precise type system for static analysis that incorporates a specific subtyping relation for type refinements. We demonstrate that this system achieves soundness and strong operational correspondence with the original calculus. Furthermore, we validate the utility of our approach through a concrete implementation in a type checker, which we have tested against a suite of examples.

This paper introduces a new framework for goal-oriented motor learning that integrates reinforcement learning with inverse control. By modeling the interaction between a robot and its environment using a physics-based approach, the system generates end-effoves to direct learning. These components are then used to derive inverse models, which feed into a policy network to estimate the necessary joint movements for achieving specific tasks. We tested this method using a simulated robotic arm tasked with reaching a target position, demonstrating its effectiveness in acquiring a new policy from scratch.

This paper introduces a novel approach to modeling the quantum harmonic oscillator, which incorporates anharmonicity to explain the temperature-dependent heat capacity of an ideal gas. By deriving the model's partition function and demonstrating that it yields results consistent with the harmonic oscillator in the high-temperature limit, we show that it produces a characteristic curve of heat capacity versus temperature that aligns with experimental observations.
